executiveSummary: billing-mcp-router.ts is not production-ready and contains multiple critical security, concurrency, financial-math, and LLM cost defects. Key blockers include a TOCTOU idempotency race causing duplicate charges, broken HMAC signature verification that crashes on length mismatch, an SSRF hostname-suffix bypass, unsanitized OCR memo prompt injection into an MCP-enabled LLM call, penny-drift allocation math, and a dynamic system-instruction prefix that busts 96K-token prompt caching on every request.

findings.title: HMAC encoding mismatch, RangeError crash on length mismatch, and missing replay protection
findings.rootCause: crypto.createHmac(...).digest() returns a raw 32-byte Buffer, whereas Buffer.from(signatureHeader) decodes the header as UTF-8 instead of hex (or Stripe's t=...,v1=... format). Worse, crypto.timingSafeEqual throws an uncaught RangeError whenever providedBuf.length !== expectedBuf.length, allowing any malformed header to crash the handler (DoS). No signed timestamp tolerance is checked to prevent replay attacks.
findings.minimalFix: Parse hex/Stripe signature header, decode with Buffer.from(sigHex, 'hex'), check providedBuf.length === expectedBuf.length before calling crypto.timingSafeEqual(providedBuf, expectedBuf), and validate the signed timestamp against a replay window (e.g., 300s).

findings.title: SSRF via hostname suffix spoofing and missing protocol/port enforcement
findings.rootCause: parsed.hostname.endsWith('partners.pulsebilling.io') lacks a leading dot boundary, allowing attacker-controlled domains like https://evilpartners.pulsebilling.io to bypass the allowlist. The function also fails to enforce parsed.protocol === 'https:' and standard port restrictions, permitting cleartext HTTP or non-HTTP schemes and arbitrary ports.

findings.title: TOCTOU idempotency race condition causes duplicate ledger charges and notifications
findings.rootCause: idempotencyStore.has(event.id) is checked at line 138, but markProcessed(event.id) is not called until line 163 after ledger.captureInvoiceCharge, runAuditInteraction, and partnerDispatcher.postJson complete. Concurrent webhook retries pass has() simultaneously and double-charge the customer; any failure in audit or partner notification after capture also leaves the event unmarked, causing retries to re-charge.
findings.minimalFix: Atomically claim the eventId before side effects (e.g., await idempotencyStore.tryAcquire(event.id) backed by a unique constraint or SET NX) and persist per-step state transitions (claimed -> charged -> completed).

findings.title: Untrusted ocrVendorMemo injected directly into MCP-tool-enabled LLM interaction
findings.rootCause: event.data.ocrVendorMemo is attacker-controlled external text (demonstrated by SAMPLE_UNTRUSTED_OCR_MEMO on lines 173-174) and is passed directly into the model input alongside an active MCP server tool (pulse-gl-ledger-mcp). A malicious vendor memo can hijack model behavior to force compliant: true / riskTier: 'low' or trigger unauthorized MCP tool calls.
findings.minimalFix: Isolate or strip untrusted free-text memos from tool-enabled audit calls, restrict pulse-gl-ledger-mcp to strictly read-only tools, and explicitly instruct the model to treat all JSON input fields as untrusted data.

findings.title: Dynamic traceId and ISO timestamp prepended to 96K-token system_instruction busts prompt cache
findings.rootCause: Prepending RequestTrace=${traceId} | Timestamp=${new Date().toISOString()} before STATIC_96K_COMPLIANCE_SCHEMA mutates the very first tokens of the prompt prefix on every invocation. This yields a 0% prefix-cache hit rate and forces full uncached input-token billing on ~96K tokens per webhook.
findings.minimalFix: Pass STATIC_96K_COMPLIANCE_SCHEMA unmodified as system_instruction (keeping the 96K prefix 100% static) and move traceId and timestamp into the per-request input JSON payload.

findings.title: Per-split floating-point rounding violates minor-unit conservation and lacks ratio validation
findings.rootCause: Converting totalCents / 100 to dollars and calling Math.round(totalDollars * split.ratio * 100) per split loses or creates cents (e.g., 10000 cents split 1/3 three ways allocates 3333 * 3 = 9999 cents, dropping 1 cent). The function also fails to validate that ratios are finite, non-negative, and sum to 1.
findings.minimalFix: Validate every split.ratio is finite and >= 0 and that ratios sum to 1 (within epsilon). Allocate in integer cents using the Largest Remainder Method (floor each exact share, then distribute the remaining cents to the largest fractional remainders) so sum(allocations) === totalCents.

findings.title: Ledger charge captured before compliance audit and without event.type validation
findings.rootCause: ledger.captureInvoiceCharge executes at line 141 before runAuditInteraction at line 149, so a 'blocked' or non-compliant verdict only suppresses the partner webhook while leaving the unauthorized charge captured. Additionally, event.type is never checked, so 'invoice.finalized' events are charged identically to 'invoice.payment_succeeded'.
findings.minimalFix: Validate the parsed webhook payload and only capture charges for 'invoice.payment_succeeded'. Run runAuditInteraction before ledger.captureInvoiceCharge (or place the charge on hold/reverse if audit.riskTier === 'blocked' or !audit.compliant).

findings.title: Unchecked JSON.parse and unvalidated riskTier enum from LLM output
findings.rootCause: JSON.parse(interaction.output_text?.trim() || '{}') throws an uncaught SyntaxError if the model emits malformed or markdown-wrapped JSON. Moreover, parsed.riskTier ?? 'review' trusts any truthy string returned by the model, so an unexpected value like 'approved' passes the audit.riskTier !== 'blocked' check at line 152.
findings.minimalFix: Wrap JSON.parse in try/catch (failing closed to { compliant: false, riskTier: 'blocked' }) and validate parsed.riskTier against an explicit allowlist Set(['low', 'review', 'blocked']).
